intro: Compact groups are useful only when they are also separated from alternatives. Silhouette scores compare within-cluster distance with the nearest other group.
task: Compute per-observation Euclidean silhouette scores and their mean for a supplied clustering.
requirements: points has shape (n,d), n>=3. labels contains n integer-valued IDs in [0,n-1] and must represent between two and n-1 distinct clusters.
For a nonsingleton observation, a is mean distance to other members of its cluster and b is the smallest mean distance to any other cluster. Score=(b-a)/max(a,b).
A singleton gets zero. If a=b=0, also use zero. Return {"scores": vector, "mean": scalar}; exclude the observation itself only from its own-cluster mean.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.body: Exclude self-distance from a, and handle a singleton before attempting to average an empty group.

explanation: A silhouette compares the average distance within the assigned group with the best competing group. Values near one indicate favorable separation; negative values indicate a closer alternative.
A singleton lacks a within-group comparison, so this exercise assigns it zero. Including self-distance in a larger group would artificially reduce a and inflate the score.
